Verdict: ACCEPT, under the stated hypothesesThe repaired notes now establish one coherent conditional compensation theorem:
$$D_C
=
2+2n+\Phi_C+A_C+D'_C,$$
where: $D_C$  is the original physical no-endpoint deficit in the cavity; $D'_C\ge 0$  is the shifted-partition no-endpoint deficit; $n$  is the number of fully enclosed positive sources besides the root; $\Phi_C$  is the signed physical singleton-end flux of complete combs that may escape; $A_C\ge 0$  is the additional phase slack from fully enclosed perpendicular sources.For a genuinely closed cavity, every endpoint component meeting the cavity is contained in it, so  $\Phi_C=0$ . The result becomes
$$D_C\ge 2(n+1),$$
and the original whole-receiver ledger then gives the stated coefficient-one bound on the covered class.I find no genuine counterexample inside the repaired hypotheses. The previously identified failures have been removed by explicit phase restrictions, boundary cases, component quantification, shifted-label forcing, normalization preservation, and the all- $a$  interface bounds.There are two wording qualifications, discussed below, but neither invalidates the compensation theorem.1. Component containment and the two partitionsThis part is now sufficient.The repaired closed-cavity hypothesis quantifies over every endpoint component meeting  $C$ :every such component, without exception for unlisted components, is contained in  $C$  and is either a complete straight comb or one of the prescribed positive sources.That closes the earlier loophole in which an unlisted endpoint component could enter the cavity and invalidate the receiver count. A component escaping through the open side is explicitly outside the closed theorem.The geometric containment argument for the receivers is also adequate without adding a support-envelope hypothesis.The cavity is
$$C=\{2,\ldots,r+1\}\times\{1,\ldots,w-2\},
\qquad r=2h+2.$$
Its row interval consists of complete physical row pairs
$$(2,3),(4,5),\ldots,(r,r+1),$$
and its column interval consists of complete original column pairs because  $w-2$  is even. Thus every original physical square containing an endpoint of a component in  $C$  is wholly contained in  $C$ .After the two extreme columns are deleted, the remaining interval
$$\{2,\ldots,w-3\}$$
is likewise a union of complete shifted column pairs. Therefore every shifted square containing an endpoint is wholly contained in  $C$  as well.This is the relevant fact. A support that forces a label may lie outside  $C$ ; the support itself does not need to belong to the receiver. The revised note handles exactly that situation. For example, an outside axial support can force a corner inside the final shifted endpoint square to be blank. That does not spoil receiver containment.So I do not find a missing support-clearance assumption here. Requiring every forcing support to lie inside  $C$  would be unnecessarily strong.Tile ownership then gives the required unique ownership in both partitions: a square containing endpoints cannot contain endpoints from two distinct endpoint components.2. The exact  $2h$  boundary selection countThe boundary count is correct and now includes the previously omitted rows.On each extreme column of  $C$ , the prescribed inside supports occur at
$$3,5,\ldots,r-1,$$
which gives exactly  $h$  selected sites per extreme column and  $2h$  selected sites in total.The proof now correctly handles all remaining rows:At row  $2$ , the inside support in row  $3$  already sees its intended arm endpoint. An occupied site at row  $2$  would give that support a second occupied neighbor.At each even row  $4,6,\ldots,r$ , the preceding inside support in row  $q-1$  excludes occupancy at row  $q$ .At row  $r+1$ , the axial support adjacent to the arm tip excludes occupancy.The same feasibility argument excludes endpoints as well as selections. Thus the two extreme columns contribute exactly  $2h$  selections and no endpoints.The tile counts are
$$N=\frac{(h+1)(w-2)}2,
\qquad
N'=\frac{(h+1)(w-4)}2,$$
so
$$N-N'=h+1.$$
Using the removal of  $2h$  selections,
$$\begin{aligned}
D_C-D'_C
&=
2(N-N')-2h+E_C-E'_C\\
&=
2(h+1)-2h+E_C-E'_C\\
&=
2+E_C-E'_C.
\end{aligned}$$
This is the exact boundary term. It is not merely a lower bound.3. Parallel positive sources: the shifted charge is  $-1$ Under the repaired positive-phase hypotheses, the shifted raw excess of every enclosed parallel positive source is indeed always
$$E'_K=-1$$
in every retaining feasible completion.The shifted receiver labels are now explicit:shifted receiver square $(p,t)$ raw excess  $t+p/2-2$ chamber square $(4,0)$  $0$ nonterminal arm square $(2,1)$  $0$ each terminal arm square $(1,1)$  $-\frac12$ Hence the chamber and nonterminal arm squares contribute zero, and the two terminal arm squares contribute
$$-\frac12-\frac12=-1.$$
The label forcing is sufficient even when a forcing support lies outside the cavity:the inside support forces the other corner in the terminal square blank;the axial support forces the final corner blank;the preceding/next inside supports fix the nonterminal arm corners;complete-component containment prevents a foreign endpoint from appearing in the receiver.The original positive physical phase still gives
$$E_K=+1.$$
Therefore
$$E_K-E'_K=1-(-1)=2$$
for every enclosed parallel positive source.Phase distinctionsThe two previously proposed counterexamples do not apply to this theorem.A one-column translation changes the original source phase and gives raw charge  $-1$ , so it is outside the prescribed  $+1$  source class. It cannot disprove the shifted  $-1$  count for the allowed phase.Likewise, a row reflection
$$r\longmapsto k-r$$
preserves the physical row-pair partition only when  $k$  is odd. An even constant maps even-starting row pairs to odd-starting pairs. The repaired note uses odd-constant row reflections for up/down opening and odd-constant column reflections for left/right symmetry. These preserve the two relevant partitions.Thus the correct statement is:the shifted source charge is  $-1$  for the declared positive phase and all retaining feasible completions, including the permitted tile-preserving reflections.It is not a statement about arbitrary translations or arbitrary reflections.4. No reuse in the complete-comb contributionThe complete-comb contribution is also sound.In either partition:an aligned comb consists of  $(p,t)=(2,1)$  receiver tiles, each with raw excess zero;a misaligned comb has two singleton end tiles of types  $(1,1)$  and  $(1,2)$ , whose raw excesses are  $-\frac12$  and  $+\frac12$ ;the middle tiles have raw excess zero.Therefore every complete comb has total raw excess zero in both partitions.The use of whole receivers prevents the half-unit at a saturated singleton end from being counted as an independent donor. The original whole-receiver correction is assigned once to the complete component, exactly as in the established receiver ledger.Tile ownership also prevents two endpoint components from sharing a receiver square. Thus the component excess decomposition does not reuse an endpoint tile or assign one raw correction to two components.5. The perpendicular-source phase formulaThe new formula
$$E'_K=1-w+\ell+q$$
is correct under the declared orientation and phase.Let the perpendicular source occupy rows  $u,\ldots,v$ , with
$$w=v-u+1,$$
and chamber columns  $c,c+1$ . The shifted receiver squares divide into interior row bands and two end caps.Write  $a_u$  and  $a_v$  for the selected outer-flank sites in the two cap rows. Then
$$\ell
=
\ell_{\mathrm{interior}}+a_u+a_v.$$
Interior row bandsThere are
$$\frac{w-2}{2}$$
interior physical row bands.In each such band, the two shifted endpoint squares have  $p=2$ . The left square has  $a$  selected sites on the outer flank  $L$ , and the right square has  $b$  selected sites on the inner flank  $I$ . Their combined raw excess is
$$(2+a/2-2)+(2+b/2-2)$$
when written per vertex, or equivalently, in the note’s doubled bookkeeping,
$$-2+a+b.$$
Summing all interior bands gives
$$-(w-2)+\ell_{\mathrm{interior}}+q.$$
Upper and lower cap bandsEach cap has one chamber-side shifted square with

or

Its raw excess is therefore
$$-\frac12+a_u

-\frac12+a_v.$$
The arm-side square in each cap has  $(p,t)=(2,1)$ , hence raw excess zero.The two caps contribute
$$-1+a_u+a_v.$$
Combining the interior and cap contributions gives
$$\begin{aligned}
E'_K
&=
-(w-2)+\ell_{\mathrm{interior}}+q-1+a_u+a_v\\
&=
1-w+\ell+q.

The original positive source phase gives
$$E_K=1.$$
Consequently,
$$\Gamma_K
=
E_K-E'_K
=
w-\ell-q.$$

$$\ell\le \frac w2.$$
Every site on
$$L=\{(r,c-1):u\le r\le v\}$$
is adjacent to a chamber endpoint. Two consecutive selected sites on  $L$  would therefore each have a second occupied neighbor. Pairing the  $w$  flank sites into adjacent pairs gives at most one selection per pair.The inner-flank bound is also valid:
$$q\le \frac{w-4}{2}.$$
The first site of  $I$ ,
$$(u+1,c+2),$$
is adjacent both to the chamber endpoint  $(u+1,c+1)$  and to the upper-arm endpoint  $(u,c+2)$ . It cannot be selected. $$q\le \frac{w-4}{2}.$$

$$\ell+q
\le
\frac w2+\frac{w-4}{2}
=
w-2,$$

$$\ell=\frac w2,

q=\frac{w-4}{2},

\Gamma_K=2.$$
